arc: From the pre-cosmic clash between Light and Darkness, the teaching follows the mingling-state down into the molding of Adam in the Deep and ends with Adam eating from the corrupt tree so that his natural eyes are opened in the mingled state.
reading:
Although heavily damaged, the teaching follows a single recognizable arc: it carries the reader from the cosmic war between Light and Darkness, through the mingling that resulted, down into the molding of the first natural man, and ends at the moment Adam eats and his eyes open. Read correspondentially, this is the standard story of how the proprium comes to be formed and how the natural understanding is first awakened — not in pure light, but in the mingled state.

The opening fragments name the Darkness and "the mystery of the clash" — the cosmic war the Darkness unleashed forth. In the doctrine of correspondences this is not a literal battle in space but the inner truth that self-love, by its nature, rises against divine good; falsity-from-evil cannot rest in itself but must assault the Light. The "great war" is therefore the perpetual aggression of the proprium against influx, and "the Darkness unleashed forth" names the moment when self-love passes from latent disorder into active opposition.

Out of that clash comes the mingling. "Through their joining, they were drawn up into this cosmos" describes how the powers of Darkness, by their very assault on the Light, were caught and lifted into this world — the present arena of mingled truth and falsity. This is the precise correspondential meaning of "cosmos" in the lexicon: the world of mingled state, where light is bound in darkness and must be sorted. The next surviving line confirms it: something of the Light — almost certainly the sons or seeds of the Light, the dispersed Living Soul — now dwells within those darkened powers in order to refine the Light out of them. The whole cosmos is here being described as a refinery: the falsity that tried to seize the Light has itself become the medium through which the Light is now purified.

The teaching then turns to the agency that generates corrupt forms within this mingling. It names "the Erring itself, with its bringing-forth" — Error personified as a cosmic principle, paired with a generative act. This is Hyle / the Enthumesis of Death in her function as the corrupt matrix: the false counterpart of the Mother of Life, who does not bring forth living truth but miscarried likenesses. Her "bringing-forth" sets the stage for what comes next.

What she brings forth, in cooperation with the Deep (the hells, the depth of falsity-from-evil), is the molding of Adam — "Adam the first[-formed]." Here the lexicon is decisive: Adam is not innocent humanity but the natural man as molded, the proprium in its first formation, the human shape into which divine truth has been sealed but in mingled corruption. The molding happens in the Deep because the natural man, considered in himself, is fashioned from below: shaped by Saklas the demiurge of self-love out of the materials Hyle provides. The Living Soul is sealed inside this molded form, which is exactly why Adam is salvageable at all — but the form itself is a corrupt vessel.

The teaching ends at the act that defines this whole molded condition: "from which Adam ate, and his eyes saw forth." The tree from which Adam eats is the bitter tree — the perception-tree whose fruit is the works of corrupt affection, the taste of disordered love. When Adam eats from it, his eyes are opened, but they are opened in the mingled state. This is the natural understanding awakening to itself: an intellect that now sees, but sees through the mingling, sees by a light filtered through Darkness. It is the birth of the proprium-mind, the eye that is open and yet is the eye blinded — open to the cosmos, closed to the inmost.

Read as one movement, then, the teaching tells how falsity's assault on Light ended by drawing falsity itself up into a refinery; how Error, working with the Deep, molded Adam as the first natural form in which captive Light could be held; and how that molded man, eating from the corrupt tree, received the kind of sight proper to his mingled condition. It is a creation-fall fragment in the strict correspondential sense: not the origin of human beings, but the origin of the proprium — and of the open-eyed natural understanding which that proprium calls knowledge.
